title: staged-private-upgrade-orchestrator-with-delta-health-probes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a staging-first upgrade orchestrator for Private (VPC) control planes that performs version-aware, delta-safe canary promotions with lightweight synthetic traffic probes and Terraform-driven IaC gating. This ticket focuses on the orchestration layer, preflight checks, and health delta probes ("probe diffs") that compare baseline vs candidate control plane behavior before promoting a version. The system must be usable by Private customers during reserved maintenance windows and integrate with existing Terraform modules and the control plane operator API.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible terraform workflow (plan/apply) exists that can create a 'canary slice' of 1-3 tenants and deploy control plane version X+1 alongside X without affecting global traffic.
Automated preflight validates operator compatibility matrix, CRD schema diffs, and migration scripts and surfaces blocking errors in Terraform plan output.

Delta health probes execute synthetic requests (control-plane admin + light inference path) and produce a delta report within 5 minutes comparing latency, error-rate, and config drift between baseline and candidate.
Roll-forward policy: automated promotion to next cohort succeeds only if delta regressions are within thresholds; otherwise orchestrator triggers automated rollback and owner notification.
Integration tests and a blue-green shadow run documented and passing in staging before rollout to production private clusters.
Terraform module changes are backward-compatible for older customers and include a one-click revert using state tagging.
Observability: dashboards and alerts for canary runs (latency P95, HTTP 5xx, reconciliation failures) created in the Console release 'private-upgrades-2026.04'.
implementation_steps: Design the 'canary slice' concept: tenant selection heuristics, capacity quota, and traffic isolation model.
Extend terraform/private-modules to support dual-controlplane deployment (version pinning and side-by-side operator instances) with minimal network changes.
Create preflight checks: CRD schema diff tool, operator compatibility verifier, and migration dry-run harness.
Implement delta health probes: lightweight synthetic scenarios (admin API, small generation, KV cache warmup) and aggregator that computes deltas vs baseline.
Orchestrator logic: staged cohorts, gating rules, automated rollback triggers, and integration with notification channels (Slack, PagerDuty).
Add telemetry: record canary-run metrics to Console and tag runs with terraform apply IDs for traceability.
End-to-end test: run on private-staging with 3 tenants; iterate on thresholds and failure modes.
Write runbook and operator guide for on-call and SEs; link to terraform usage examples.
Code review and security review; merge terraform modules and orchestration controller.
Schedule pilot with an internal private customer, run one controlled upgrade window, collect learnings, and follow up.
rollback_plan: Immediate rollback to previous control plane version on failure threshold breach (automated via orchestrator).
If rollback fails, execute emergency revert terraform state tag to restore routing and re-run baseline operator reconciliation.
Notify on-call SRE, SE contact, and account owner; open incident bridge with context from delta report.
If tenant-level rollback needed, isolate and migrate affected tenant to baseline instance using live data path mirroring.
Postmortem and automated mitigation (e.g., disable automatic promos) until root cause fixed.
telemetry_and_metrics: Canary run ID, start/end timestamps, cohort size, and terraform apply ID
Latency P50/P95/P99 for synthetic probe across baseline and candidate
Error rates (5xx, reconcilation errors) and consumer-visible failures
Operator reconciliation duration and CRD migration warnings
Delta score metric (normalized composite of latency, errors, and recon failures)
Console dashboard links and alert rules (alert if delta_score > 0.15 or 5xx spike > 1%)
risks: Side-by-side operator instances increase resource consumption; private customers with tight quotas may experience capacity pressure.
Schema migrations may require coordinated data migrations not captured by terraform plan; these need explicit migration hooks.
False negatives in synthetic probes could pass a bad build — probe coverage must be maintained and expanded over time.
Terraform state complexity increases with dual deployments; operator mistakes can lead to orphaned resources unless state tagging is robust.
Automated rollbacks could cascade if not rate-limited; need guardrails to prevent flip-flop upgrades.
